overview: Monaco is a tiny city-state on the Mediterranean coast, surrounded on land by France. It is the second-smallest country in the world, after Vatican City, and one of the most densely populated. Monaco is a principality ruled by the Grimaldi family, and it is famous for its casino in Monte Carlo and the Monaco Grand Prix.

geography.text: Monaco is squeezed onto a narrow, hilly strip of coast at the foot of the Alps, so its buildings are tall and packed closely together. Parts of the country have been built on land reclaimed from the sea. It has no farmland and no rivers or lakes of any size.

history.text: The Grimaldi family seized the fortress of Monaco in 1297, reportedly with a soldier disguised as a monk, and has ruled it almost ever since. Monaco lost most of its land in the 1800s, but the Monte Carlo casino made it rich. Prince Rainier III's marriage to the film star Grace Kelly in 1956 made it world-famous.

events.title: The Grimaldis arrive
events.text: François Grimaldi captures the fortress of Monaco.

events.title: Treaty with France
events.text: Monaco gives up most of its land to France in return for recognition of its independence.

events.title: The casino
events.text: The company that runs the Monte Carlo casino is founded.

events.title: First Grand Prix
events.text: The first Monaco Grand Prix is held on the city's streets.

events.title: A royal wedding
events.text: Prince Rainier III marries the American actress Grace Kelly.

government.text: Monaco is a constitutional monarchy ruled by the Grimaldi family. The Prince holds strong powers and appoints a Minister of State to lead the government. The National Council, elected every five years, passes laws and the budget. France is responsible for Monaco's defence.

economy.text: Monaco is famous for its wealth. There is no income tax for most residents, which has drawn many very rich people. Tourism, banking, property and the Monte Carlo casino are the main businesses. It uses the euro.

culture.text: Monaco is the second-smallest country in the world and the most densely populated. Its Oceanographic Museum, built into the cliff in 1910, was once run by the explorer Jacques Cousteau. Most residents are foreigners; Monégasque citizens are a small minority.

items.title: Oceanographic Museum
items.text: Opened in 1910 on the cliff above the sea.

items.title: Monte Carlo Casino
items.text: Opened in the 1860s and made Monaco rich.

sport.text: The Monaco Grand Prix, raced through the city's narrow streets since 1929, is the most famous race in Formula 1. AS Monaco plays in the French football league and has won it several times.

items.title: Monaco Grand Prix
items.text: Held on the streets of Monte Carlo since 1929.

items.title: Charles Leclerc
items.text: The Ferrari driver, born in Monaco, won his home Grand Prix in 2024.

didYouKnow: Monaco is smaller than Central Park in New York.
Monaco has more police officers per person than almost any other country.

keyPeople.name: Grace Kelly
keyPeople.text: The Hollywood star married Prince Rainier III in 1956.

keyPeople.name: Charles Leclerc
keyPeople.text: Formula 1 driver for Ferrari, born in Monaco.
